grh_6e47416f53331d653f89.title: Diagnosis After Death
paragraphs: While Dr. Alexander Webb is temporarily covering Dr. Christian's practice, state senator Fredericks is found dead in the street after appearing to stagger like a drunk. The senator's widow Margaret privately threatens Webb, saying she heard him quarrel with her husband shortly before the death and will accuse him of murder unless he helps prevent an investigation that could expose family scandals. Webb had opposed the senator's plan to release and abandon his violently insane brother, giving Margaret a plausible motive to use against him. At the medical inquiry, needle scars first suggest that the senator may have been a drug addict, but Webb notices that the fresh injection was high on the right arm, an awkward place for the right-handed senator to inject himself. He concludes the senator was diabetic, that the marks came from insulin, and that a family member sometimes gave the arm injections. An excessive dose would also explain the senator's staggering before death as insulin shock rather than drunkenness. As Webb works through the evidence, Margaret breaks down and confesses that she deliberately gave her husband the fatal overdose because she hated him. Her attempt to coerce and frame Webb collapses under the medical evidence.

The structured record associates the broadcast with [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]]. Credited performers include Jean Hersholt, Claude Rains, and Helen Claire. grh_6e02d7c76ade8dd080b6.title: Blind Boy Story
paragraphs: Dr. Christian saves a mysterious man who has taken poison and is determined to try again rather than face the disgrace and consequences waiting for him at home. Instead of turning him over to anyone, the doctor asks for a few more hours and takes him on an early-morning call to a poor farm family. There the man meets fourteen-year-old Robert, blind from birth with congenital cataracts, whose family has sacrificed for years to pay for an operation. Dr. Christian removes Robert's bandages and the boy sees his mother, his dog, his home and the dawn for the first time, declaring the world wonderful. Witnessing that joy gives the despairing man a new perspective. He abandons his plan to die and chooses to return home and face his troubles, while Dr. Christian compares life to a game that can be started again after a loss.

paragraphs: A humorous autobiographical adaptation of Donald Hough's Captain Retread follows a middle-aged World War I veteran returning to uniform as an Air Force captain. grh_6e00914749e42fab9953.title: The Norton Nose
paragraphs: A truck accident badly mangles young Pamela Norton's prominent family nose, and the reconstruction becomes a comic battle over identity. Pamela privately begs for a prettier nose, while formidable Aunt Augusta insists that the surgeon reproduce the ancestral Norton profile exactly from an old family miniature. Dr. Christian and the plastic surgeon refuse to turn Pamela into a museum piece and instead reconstruct a natural-looking nose suited to the young woman she actually is. The result helps free Pamela from years of embarrassment, and her romance with Mike Clancy moves toward marriage despite Augusta's outrage over the altered family landmark.
